paras: The threatened lynching of Fullberg was an episode in Montana Territory in September 1888, when a man named Fullberg came to the military post at Fort Shaw with his family and asked protection from a body of vigilantes he said meant to lynch him. The commanding officer declined to protect him, calling it a matter for the civil authorities, and no later outcome was reported.

The quarrel went back about eight years, to an alleged theft of horses from a ranchman named Dunn. According to Fullberg, men had tried to hang him at the time of the alleged theft. He had since been tried at Fort Benton for the alleged theft and acquitted.

On September 21, 1888, Fullberg arrived at Fort Shaw, saying that vigilantes headed by Dunn were "trying to catch and lynch him" for the old horse theft. He had brought his family with him and refused to return home without protection. The commanding officer said he could not provide it, "as the case is one for the civil authorities."
No report of what became of Fullberg, of any action by civil officers, or of arrests among the vigilantes appears in the coverage.

The episode is known from a single special dispatch from Helena, dated September 21, which the St. Paul Daily Globe printed on its front page the next day. Under the headline "Under Uncle Sam's Wing," with the subhead "A Ranchman Seeks Protection From Judge Lynch," the Globe called Fullberg a ranchman and presented the lynching threat as his claim. The brief dispatch set his acquittal beside the note that Dunn, "the leader of the vigilantes," was the man who had lost the horses, and it gave no race for anyone involved.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of Fullberg
bases: A body of vigilantes was reported to be trying to catch and lynch Fullberg on a horse-theft accusation; no one was killed, so this is a threatened lynching (A1).

No one was killed: Fullberg reached Fort Shaw with his family and asked protection from vigilantes who, by his own account, wanted to lynch him for an old horse theft (A1); the size of the 'body of vigilantes' is not given.
One Helena special to the St. Paul Globe is the only report found, and its core claim (that the vigilantes meant to lynch him) is attributed to Fullberg himself (A1).

accounts.label: Fullberg's claim, via Helena special
accounts.gist: Fullberg said vigilantes led by Dunn were trying to catch and lynch him for a horse theft of eight years earlier, as they had tried to hang him then; the dispatch adds that he had been tried and acquitted at Fort Benton.

framing.detail: The Globe's headline 'Under Uncle Sam's Wing' cast Fullberg as 'A Ranchman' seeking protection from 'Judge Lynch' and gave his claim, his acquittal and Dunn's grievance without comment.

threatened: a reported pursuit with intent to lynch, with no seizure or assault in this episode (an attempt to hang him is said to have occurred eight years earlier)
